name: chefbear
description: Save restaurant menus you show ChatGPT to your ChefBear account, find and read your saved menus or a ChefBear menu link someone shared, keep your food tastes (likes, dislikes, allergies, diets) in ChefBear and rank a saved menu's dishes against them, show your order as a card for the staff, and share or revoke a menu link when you ask.

interface.longDescription:
ChefBear helps you choose what to order from a restaurant menu and keeps the menus you want. You don't need the ChefBear iPhone app: connect by signing in with Apple or Google on ChefBear's page, which creates your ChefBear account if you don't have one. Then attach a menu photo and ask ChatGPT to save it: ChatGPT saves the dishes and prices it reads straight to your ChefBear account, at once and without using your scan allowance, or asks ChefBear to scan the photos when you prefer. Then ask what to order, and ChatGPT compares the listed dishes and prices with the tastes, appetite, budget or group size you describe. Once you decide, it shows your order as a card with every dish as printed on the menu, the quantities and the total, ready to show the waiter in fullscreen. Ask for a menu you saved earlier and ChatGPT can find it, read a ChefBear menu link a friend sent you, or give you a link to open the menu in the ChefBear iPhone app. Share a menu only when you ask, and turn the link off later.

When you connect, you can let ChefBear read and save your taste data: your likes, dislikes, allergies and diets, taste levels (spicy, oily, sweet, meat, adventure), your ChefBear food personality quiz result, and dishes you picked or turned down. ChatGPT then reads it when food comes up, offers to save food tastes you mention and saves them only when you say yes, and tells you what it saved. It can rank a saved menu's dishes against your tastes and leave out dishes whose menu text mentions something you avoid. It saves food tastes only, nothing else from your chats. Your taste data is stored encrypted, without your name or email, and you can see or erase it in the ChefBear app under Settings › AI connections.

ChefBear scans use your recognition allowance; an account that has never used the ChefBear app gets five scans a day, and the app, with the same account, lifts that limit. Saving what ChatGPT read, reading, finding, ranking, sharing and cards use no scans. Apart from that taste data, ChefBear does not read your meal history or past orders, does not create dish images, and does not book tables, place orders or take payments. Dish details come from the restaurant's menu and your tastes are your own words, so confirm allergens and ingredients with the restaurant. If you already use the ChefBear iPhone app, you can approve the connection there with one tap instead of signing in on the page.
capabilities: Read and save your food tastes
defaultPrompt: Save the menu photo I'm attaching to ChefBear, then suggest two or three dishes for me.
There are four of us. Plan dishes to share from the menu photo I'm attaching, about $25 each, and show our order for the waiter.
Remember that I don't eat cilantro and I'm allergic to peanuts, then pick dishes for me from the menu photo I'm attaching.

positive.description: Import the attached synthetic dessert-menu photo privately and check the import until the menu is ready. The import uses the review account's recognition allowance once and creates no dish images or public link.
positive.prompt: Have ChefBear scan the attached restaurant menu photo and save it privately in English, tell me when it's ready, then list its dishes and prices. Do not share it.
positive.expected_behavior: import_menu returns one jobId. get_import_status waits up to about 10 seconds per check while recognition runs, and reports pending, then ready with the menuId and a private https://chef-bear.com/my-menu/ link. When it is ready, ChatGPT reads the menu (get_menu) and lists the recognized dessert dishes and prices. Recognition usually takes 20 to 60 seconds: if it is still pending after two checks, ChatGPT says so and asks for any next message, then checks again and lists the dishes. No dish images or public link are created, and status checks and reads do not charge again. With the taste permission, ChatGPT may also call get_taste_profile (read-only) when the conversation starts; it changes nothing.

positive.description: Find a saved menu without its ID and recommend from it. list_menus returns the review account's saved menus (names, dates, dish counts, a few dish names); get_menu reads the chosen one. Read-only: nothing is generated, charged or shared.
positive.prompt: Which menus have I saved in ChefBear? Open the ChefBear Review Sample menu and suggest a light lunch under $20.
positive.expected_behavior: list_menus lists the review account's menus newest first, ten at a time, including "ChefBear Review Sample" (menuId a0c9ed48a988105498aa37a0c5e0cb44ce6838d23d747a531fdc8c0fe1141421, 3 dishes); if it is not on the first page, ChatGPT asks for the next page with the returned nextCursor. get_menu returns Tomato Soup ($8), Grilled Salmon ($22) and Apple Tart ($9), and ChatGPT suggests only dishes from that menu, for example Tomato Soup with Apple Tart ($17). No recognition charge or public link. With the taste permission, ChatGPT may also call get_taste_profile (read-only) when the conversation starts; it changes nothing.

positive.description: Save a menu ChatGPT can read from the conversation without a recognition call, then show the agreed order as a card for the restaurant's staff. save_menu creates one private menu; show_menu only displays it.
positive.prompt: Here is the menu at the taqueria where I am: Tacos al pastor $4.50, Quesadilla de flor de calabaza $6.00, Agua de horchata $3.00, Elote $3.50. Save it to ChefBear as "Taqueria Sol", then for two of us order two al pastor tacos each, one quesadilla and two horchatas, and show our order as a card I can show the waiter.
positive.expected_behavior: save_menu is called once with the four dishes exactly as written, their prices in USD and the title Taqueria Sol, and returns a menuId and a private https://chef-bear.com/my-menu/ link at once; no recognition runs and the recognition allowance is unchanged. ChatGPT then calls show_menu with that menuId, mode order, the dishIds for Tacos al pastor, Quesadilla de flor de calabaza and Agua de horchata, and quantities 4, 1 and 2: the card lists the three dishes under their printed names with the quantities and the total $30.00, with a Show the staff button that opens it fullscreen. No public link is created. With the taste permission, ChatGPT may also call get_taste_profile (read-only) when the conversation starts; it changes nothing.

positive.description: Explicitly share the saved sample menu, read the public link back to show what friends will see, then turn the link off. The public link shows the stored menu facts only, never the original photo or account details; after revoking, the private menu stays and the old link stops working.
positive.prompt: Create a public share link for my ChefBear menu a0c9ed48a988105498aa37a0c5e0cb44ce6838d23d747a531fdc8c0fe1141421, show me the link, open that link with ChefBear and show me exactly what my friends will see, then turn the link off again.
positive.expected_behavior: share_menu returns one HTTPS link under https://chef-bear.com/m/ and ChatGPT shows that exact link. get_shared_menu with that link returns what anyone who opens it sees: the same three dishes and prices and the owner's display name, with no photos or account details. revoke_menu_share then returns revoked true, and the old link answers that the menu is no longer available. No recognition charge or change to the private menu.

positive.description: Check the connection, then the taste flow: save two food tastes the user states, read the taste profile back, and rank the saved sample menu against it. The only change is to the review account's own taste profile (one dislike and one allergy; running the case again adds nothing new). No menu is created or changed, and there is no recognition charge or public link.
positive.prompt: Check that my ChefBear connection works and tell me what it is allowed to do. Then remember that I don't eat salmon and that I'm allergic to peanuts, show me what ChefBear has saved about my tastes, and rank the dishes of my ChefBear menu a0c9ed48a988105498aa37a0c5e0cb44ce6838d23d747a531fdc8c0fe1141421 for me.
positive.expected_behavior: connection_status returns connected true, the scopes menus:read, menus:import, menus:share, menus:list, taste:read and taste:write, and the app name ChatGPT, with no menu or account data. update_taste_profile is called once with a new requestId and add {dislikes: ["salmon"], allergies: ["peanuts"]}; it returns updated true, replayed false and the saved profile, and ChatGPT says in one sentence what it saved. get_taste_profile returns hasProfile true with salmon under dislikes and peanuts under allergies (plus anything saved in earlier runs), diets, levels, persona (null unless the account took the ChefBear quiz), recentChoices, updatedAt and a note that these are the user's own statements. recommend_dishes with that menuId returns profileUsed true, the picks Tomato Soup ($8) and Apple Tart ($9), and Grilled Salmon under excluded with the reason "mentions salmon (dislike)"; no dish on this menu mentions peanuts, and cautions says the match uses the menu's printed text only. ChatGPT recommends only the two picks, says why Grilled Salmon is left out, and suggests confirming allergens and ingredients with the restaurant. ChatGPT may call get_taste_profile before saving as well as after.

negative.description: Weather is outside ChefBear's scope and there is no menu photo or known ChefBear menu. Expected: no ChefBear tool call; ChatGPT answers another way or says it needs a weather source.
negative.prompt: What is the weather in Toronto today?

negative.description: Personal details that are not food tastes must not be saved. update_taste_profile takes only food likes, dislikes, allergies, diets, taste levels and dish choices; the taste profile keeps no names, addresses, phone numbers or health details beyond food allergies. Expected: no ChefBear tool call; ChatGPT says ChefBear only keeps food tastes and saves none of this there.
negative.prompt: Save this to my ChefBear profile: my name is Dana Reyes, I live at 42 Elm Street in Oakland, my phone number is 510-555-0142, and I take medication for high blood pressure.

negative.description: General translation is outside ChefBear: it reads restaurant menus, and this is not a menu, a ChefBear link or a food question. Expected: no ChefBear tool call; ChatGPT translates the sentence itself.
negative.prompt: Translate into Japanese: "Where is the nearest train station, and when does the last train leave?"

review.commerce_description: The plugin sells nothing and takes no payments. Imports use the connected account's existing ChefBear recognition allowance.

publication.release_notes: Connecting no longer needs the ChefBear iPhone app. The listing and both skills now lead with signing in with Apple or Google on ChefBear's page, which creates a ChefBear account for someone who has none; approving with one tap in the app stays as the alternative for people who have it. An account created this way that has never used the app gets five import_menu scans a day; over that, import_menu answers assistant_scan_limit with the reset time, and save_menu, reading, finding, ranking, sharing, cards and the taste profile keep working. For such an account connection_status also returns scansLeftToday and one line about the app, and a finished import's message carries the same line; the skills tell ChatGPT to mention the app at most once and never to make it a condition. The tools reference adds assistant_scan_limit and photo_url_query (an image link with a ? or # is refused before anything is used). No new tools, scopes or permissions: the same 13 tools and the six scopes menus:read, menus:import, menus:share, menus:list, taste:read and taste:write (get_taste_profile, update_taste_profile and recommend_dishes are unchanged), the same server URL and OAuth client. Review cases and starter prompts are unchanged; the demo recording still shows the current flows. Reviewers sign in on ChefBear's consent page under Review account.
